body: In 1913, Timothy Drew — reborn as Noble Drew Ali — founded a movement that fused Islam, Freemasonry, Theosophy, and a reclaimed Moorish ancestry into a single scripture: the Circle Seven Koran.

The Red Seven of its cover was never a simple emblem. It gathered astrological, Masonic, and esoteric number symbolism into a single sign of national and spiritual restoration for a people the movement insisted had been made to forget their true origin.
This essay reads the Moorish Science Temple as a serious esoteric project in its own right — a twentieth-century American scripture built from the same hidden architecture this press exists to study.
